terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo types a few keys into your debounce and throttle with real timers.

tasks.title: Debounce with injectable timers
tasks.description:
Implement `debounce(fn, waitMs, options?)` in `src/debounce.ts` with its default options.

- Each call restarts a wait of `waitMs`. When `waitMs` passes with no new call, `fn` runs once with the arguments of the latest call.
- Start and clear timers only through `options.timers` (`setTimeout` and `clearTimeout`). Without that option, use `realTimers` from `src/timers.ts`.
- The returned function also needs `cancel` and `flush` methods to type-check. They are tested in task 2.

The check passes fake timers and logs the pretend time and arguments of every run of `fn`. It also tries the function with real timers.
nextSteps: Read `src/timers.ts` and pick `timers` out of the options.
Keep the latest arguments and the current timer in variables of the closure.
On every call, clear the old timer and start a new one.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and look at the first block.
hints: The returned function needs memory between calls: a closure over a couple of `let` variables is enough.
If you call the global `setTimeout`, the check's fake clock never fires your timer. Use `timers.setTimeout` and `timers.clearTimeout`.
A function is an object, so you can attach `cancel` and `flush` to it before returning it. Empty bodies are fine for now.

tasks.title: Leading, trailing, cancel and flush
tasks.description:
Add the options and methods to `debounce`. A burst is a run of calls with gaps shorter than `waitMs`. It ends `waitMs` after its last call.

- `leading` (default `false`): the first call of a burst runs `fn` at once.
- `trailing` (default `true`): when the burst ends, `fn` runs with the latest arguments, but only if some call in the burst has not run yet. A burst of one leading call does not run twice.
- `cancel()`: drops any pending call and ends the burst.
- `flush()`: if a call is pending, runs it now. Either way the burst ends and no timer is left.

The check replays bursts with each combination of options, cancels and flushes at different moments, and calls again afterwards.
nextSteps: Add a variable that says whether a burst is in progress.
Run `fn` at once for the first call of a burst when `leading` is set.
Only keep arguments as pending when that call did not already run.
Write `cancel` and `flush` so both leave no burst and no timer behind.
hints: Ask two questions on every call: is this the first call of a burst, and did this call already run?
If the leading call also stores its arguments as pending, the trailing run repeats it. Store arguments only for calls that did not run.
Write one function that ends a burst: it marks the burst over, takes the pending arguments, clears them and runs `fn` if `trailing` allows. The timer and `flush` can both call it.

tasks.title: Throttle with a trailing call
tasks.description:
Implement `throttle(fn, waitMs, options?)` in `src/throttle.ts`. It runs `fn` at most once per `waitMs` and never loses the last call.

- A call while no window is open runs `fn` at once and opens a window of `waitMs`.
- Calls while a window is open only remember their arguments. The latest wins.
- When a window closes with remembered arguments, `fn` runs with them and a new window opens straight away. Otherwise throttling stops until the next call.
- `cancel()` drops remembered arguments and closes the window.
- Timers come from `options.timers`, default `realTimers`.

The check also sends 100,000 calls one millisecond apart. `fn` must run once per window, the last call must arrive, and you may start at most two timers per window.
nextSteps: Decide what state you need: whether a window is open, and the remembered arguments.
Write what happens when a window closes.
Make a closing window open a new one when it ran `fn`.
Run the demo and look at the last block.
hints: Unlike debounce, a call during a window does not touch the timer at all.
One small function that runs `fn` and starts the window timer can serve both a fresh call and a closing window.
When the window timer fires: mark the window closed, take the remembered arguments and clear them, and if there were any, run `fn` and open a new window.
